Symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
Precautions_Management: Continue field scouting; maintain balanced nutrition and irrigation; remove severely damaged leaves.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: No pesticide needed for healthy plants; use chemicals only if a diagnosed pest/disease warrants it.

Symptoms: Leaf curling, distortion, stunting; often associated with whitefly-transmitted virus
Precautions_Management: Remove badly infected plants where appropriate; control vector populations; use clean planting material and field sanitation.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: For vector control, use only a locally registered insecticide/product according to its label and current state recommendations.

Symptoms: Circular/irregular spots on leaves that may enlarge and cause defoliation
Precautions_Management: Remove infected debris; improve air circulation; avoid prolonged leaf wetness and overhead irrigation.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: A locally registered fungicide may be used only after confirming disease and checking the current label.

Symptoms: Small white insects, honeydew, leaf yellowing/curling
Precautions_Management: Monitor undersides of leaves; remove heavily infested leaves; use integrated pest management and avoid unnecessary spraying.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Use a currently registered whitefly insecticide for chilli only at the label rate and waiting period.

Symptoms: Leaf yellowing can have multiple causes including nutrient, water, root or pest problems
Precautions_Management: Do not diagnose from colour alone; inspect roots, irrigation, nutrition and pests before treatment.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Do not apply a pesticide based only on yellow colour; identify the cause first.

Symptoms: Brown lesions/spots on leaves, often with yellow halos
Precautions_Management: Use balanced nutrition, avoid plant stress, maintain field sanitation and monitor disease development.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Use a fungicide only after confirming brown spot and following the current registered label/advisory.

Disease_Name: Rice leaf smut / smut-like leaf symptoms
Symptoms: Dark smut-like lesions on leaves
Precautions_Management: Remove/manage infected plant debris and maintain balanced crop nutrition; confirm diagnosis because similar symptoms can occur in other diseases.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Do not select a pesticide from the image alone; confirm the disease and use only a currently registered rice product if recommended.

Symptoms: Water-soaked to yellowish lesions/stripes, often progressing from leaf tips
Precautions_Management: Use resistant/tolerant varieties where available, avoid excessive nitrogen, manage water and field sanitation.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Use only a locally recommended and currently registered bactericide/management product; chemical control of bacterial disease is limited.

Precautions_Management: Use clean planting material, remove infected clumps where recommended and control vectors as part of IPM.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Mosaic is viral; there is no pesticide that cures the virus. Vector management should follow local recommendations.

Symptoms: Reddish internal tissue, drying/collapse and characteristic red rot symptoms
Precautions_Management: Use healthy seed cane, resistant varieties where available, remove infected stools and improve field sanitation.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Do not rely on pesticide alone; use resistant/clean planting material and local disease-management recommendations.

Symptoms: Rust-coloured pustules/lesions on leaves

Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Use a fungicide only when locally recommended and registered for sugarcane rust.

Precautions_Management: Use resistant varieties where available, clean seed, field sanitation and avoid unnecessary leaf wetness.

Symptoms: Leaf curling, vein thickening and plant stunting
Precautions_Management: Use healthy planting material, remove infected plants where recommended and manage whitefly vectors through IPM.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: There is no pesticide that cures the virus; insecticide use is for vector management only and must follow the current label.

Symptoms: Yellowing, wilting and vascular discoloration; diagnosis should be confirmed
Precautions_Management: Use resistant varieties, crop rotation and clean planting material; avoid moving contaminated soil between fields.
Treatment_Pesticide_Information: Do not apply a pesticide solely from an image prediction; soil-borne wilt management should follow local agricultural recommendations.

Symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in stripes on leaves
Precautions_Management: Scout early, avoid conducive crop conditions where agronomically feasible and use resistant varieties where available.
